sahneler.metin: Boston's new blue glass skyscraper began losing its windows.
Suddenly huge panes fell from the tower to the street below.
Each window had two layers of glass bonded together.
The bond was too stiff to flex.
Repeated heating and cooling cracked the panes.
Plywood covered the gaps, earning the name Plywood Palace.
All ten thousand three hundred forty four panes were replaced.
A tuned mass damper was added to stop the sway.

aciklama:
Hancock Tower lost window panes that fell to the street. The cause: repeated thermal stress and oscillation cracking over-stiff bonded window units.
